title: Pastitsio (Greek Baked Pasta with Spiced Beef and Béchamel)
summary: A Greek baked pasta dish of cinnamon-spiced beef sauce and egg-bound pasta layered under a rich, golden béchamel.
equipment: large deep frying pan or wide saucepan
baking dish about 23 x 33 cm, at least 7 cm deep

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (0.8%)
ingredients.note: about 5.25 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the onion and beef
steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6-8 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute. Add the minced beef, salt and pepper, breaking it up as it cooks for 8-10 minutes, until no pink remains and all the liquid it releases has cooked away - the mince needs to reach at least 71°C right through.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Stir in the tomato purée, cinnamon, oregano and bay leaf and cook for 1-2 minutes. Warming the spices briefly in the fat before adding liquid helps bloom their flavour fully into the sauce rather than leaving it muted.

steps.title: Simmer the meat sauce
steps.text: Pour in the tinned tomatoes and water, then simmer for 25-30 minutes, until thick rather than wet. Discard the bay leaf once the sauce tastes deep and well seasoned.

steps.title: Cook and bind the pasta
steps.text: Bring 4 litres of water to the boil with the 32 g salt and cook the pasta for 2 minutes less than the packet time, since it will soften further in the oven. Drain and cool for 5 minutes, then toss with the beaten egg and 30 g of pecorino - the egg coats and binds the strands so the pasta layer holds together when the dish is sliced.

steps.title: Make the béchamel
steps.text: Melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour and cook for 1-2 minutes without letting it colour. Gradually whisk in the warm milk, then simmer, whisking constantly, for 5-6 minutes until it thickens to the consistency of custard.

steps.title: Finish the béchamel
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the nutmeg and salt, then the egg yolks and 40 g of pecorino. The yolks are what let the sauce set into a thick, golden top once baked, rather than staying runny.

steps.title: Preheat and layer
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead and butter the baking dish. Spread the egg-bound pasta in the base, cover with the meat sauce, then pour over the béchamel and scatter with the remaining cheese.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 45-50 minutes, until the top is deep golden and puffed and an instant-read thermometer in the centre reads 74°C.

steps.title: Rest before cutting
steps.text: Leave the pastitsio to rest for 30 minutes before cutting it into squares. This is essential - without it, the layers won't have set enough to hold together and it will collapse into a heap on the plate.

tips: Make sure the béchamel is genuinely thick, like custard, before it goes over the layers - a thin béchamel won't set and the dish will be sloppy when sliced.
Don't skip resting the pastitsio for the full 30 minutes; cutting it too soon is the most common reason it falls apart on the plate.
Cooking the pasta slightly under packet time keeps it from turning mushy once it's baked again in the oven.
safety: Check the centre reaches 74°C with a thermometer, especially in a deeper dish, to make sure both the beef and egg layers are fully cooked through.
storage: Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days, or can be frozen in portions for up to 2 months. Reheat in a 180°C oven, covered loosely with foil, until piping hot and the centre reaches 74°C. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
